reviewType: independent, refute not confirm; v3 successor of REJECTED v2

selfCorrection.summary: RB-DR011-CX-B1 rejected v2. I reviewed v2 and returned ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories. The blocker is real, it is in the operative grant field, and I did not look at that field on its own terms.
selfCorrection.whatV2Said: v2's whatMayBeDesigned contained a single entry, P-011-1, whose surface was 'Architecture preview that does not pretend residuals are closed' and whose bound was 'Preview docs may name residuals as open. They may not treat a green checker, an ACCEPT-STANDING instrument review, or this parent disposition as residual closure.'
selfCorrection.whyThatIsABlocker: Both the surface and the bound are prohibitions. whatMayBeDesigned is the field whose entire job is to state what becomes permitted, and in v2 it stated only what remained forbidden. Read literally it grants 'architecture preview' — an enormous surface for a row spanning identity recipes, checker standing, evidence joins, evaluation proof and the product boundary — limited only by not *saying* residuals are closed. That permits residual-dependent design so long as it stays quiet about the residuals, which is the opposite of what a parent disposition over sixteen open residuals should do. The prompt's phrase for it, 'a circular anti-closure rule instead of a bound', is exactly right: the permitted surface was defined by the prohibition and then bounded by the same prohibition.
selfCorrection.howIMissedIt: I audited the refusals exhaustively and never audited the grant. My v2 verdict checked the sixteen-residual map item by item against file 08, chased R03 down to the register's own 'do not infer acceptance from execution alone', verified the R06/R07 NARROWED scoping, and confirmed every whatThisDoesNotDo entry. All of that was sound and none of it touched whatMayBeDesigned. The dispatch's attack axes all pointed at closure, and I followed them instead of reading the operative grant field independently.
selfCorrection.howThisDiffersFromMyEarlierMisses: My previous three recorded misses were one shape — confirming a citation resolves without asking what it resolves to after the authorized act. This is a different and more basic failure: reading everything an artifact forbids and never asking what it allows. On a permission-granting instrument that is the first question, not the last.
selfCorrection.correctiveDiscipline: On any disposition, read whatMayBeDesigned first and on its own terms, before the refusals. For each entry ask two things: what does this positively authorize, and is the bound something other than a restatement of the prohibition? A bound that only repeats what is forbidden is not a bound.

advisoriesRecorded.location: recordedInputs, read against the retained remeasurementClause
advisoriesRecorded.observation: v3 removes the propertyPins field that v2 carried, while keeping the clause that depends on it. remeasurementClause still reads 'If a cited file moves, re-measure. Pins support only the named properties.' — but no properties are now named. v2's propertyPins read 'D-055 ADOPTED; file 08 Exact DR-011 residual reconciliation; D-001 DR-011 per-residual routes; D-018 naming; D-081 condition-1 row names DR-011 as the sole unresolved of the eleven'. Of those five, D-055, D-018 and the D-081 condition-1 row survive elsewhere in v3, but 'file 08 Exact DR-011 residual reconciliation' and the D-001 per-residual routes do not appear anywhere in the document.
advisoriesRecorded.whyItMatters: The file 08 pin is a whole-document digest, and the property declaration is what bounded which section it was being offered as evidence for. Without it the clause 'Pins support only the named properties' points at an empty set, so the whole-document pin is now unbounded in what it is claimed to support. This corpus has an explicit doctrine on exactly this point — freeze §7.10 warns against pinning a current value rather than a property, and file 08 carries a standing note calling whole-document pins a known defect of the citation form.
advisoriesRecorded.whyItIsNotABlocker: Nothing asserted is false, and the pin discipline is stronger overall in v3 than in v2: the new operativeDispositionPins block pins nine dispositions by path and sha256 with their owner recordings, riders, half and route, which is far more specific than the prose string it displaced. The two lost properties are recoverable from D-055 and file 08 directly. This is a regression in one field, not a defect in the disposition.
advisoriesRecorded.context: All three sibling dispositions — DR-006 v2, DR-007 v2, DR-009 v2 — carry propertyPins, as did DR-011 v2. v3 is the only one without it.
advisoriesRecorded.suggestedFix: Restore propertyPins to recordedInputs, minimally naming file 08's Exact DR-011 residual reconciliation section and D-001's per-residual routes alongside the operativeDispositionPins block; or drop the 'named properties' sentence from remeasurementClause so the document stops referring to a set it does not contain.

summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only, and the v2 predecessor is still frozen at the digest v3 pins for it. The blocker that rejected v2 is genuinely repaired, and repaired structurally rather than verbally: the circular P-011-1 is replaced by P-011-A, whose surface is 'surfaces already allowed by the pinned owner-recorded DR-002 through DR-010 dispositions and by D-002 / D-018' and whose bound is 'This parent adds no additional surface.' That is a zero-new-permission grant anchored to specific bytes — I verified all nine operativeDispositionPins against live files and all nine owner recordings as ADOPTED. The five D-055 consequences map onto that decision's clause 4 one for one, checked against the D-055 draft rather than its condensed register entry. The sixteen-residual map survives intact. My advisory is a field v3 dropped while keeping the clause that depends on it, and I have recorded a self-correction because v2's blocker was mine to catch.

The attack 'claimed repair not actually landed' and 'still a circular anti-closure rule instead of a bound' both fail. P-011-1 is gone. P-011-A's surface is defined by reference to other instruments — the nine pinned owner-recorded dispositions plus D-002 / D-018 — and its bound is 'This parent adds no additional surface. Residual-dependent recipes, schemas, identities, exits, custody, proof, checker standing, and product boundaries are not granted here.' The bound now constrains rather than restates, and it is reinforced by a new top-level field: 'Residual-dependent recipes, schemas, identities, exits, custody, proof, checker standing, and product boundaries gain no design permission from this parent disposition. Labeling a residual OPEN is not a design grant.' That last sentence is the direct answer to the circularity.

The no-new-permission claim is anchored to bytes, not prose. All nine operativeDispositionPins verify against live files: DR-002 301ea338…, DR-003 d9084d4d…, DR-004 2866dd87…, DR-005 3b50bcf1… with rider RB-DR005-V2-A1, DR-006 28fb23ec…, DR-007 53b72a91…, DR-008 8b2d2139… marked 'integration only', DR-009 5e2f6572… with rider RB-DR009-V2-A1, and DR-010 ff7a0913… marked route C. Each names its owner recording, and all nine — D-058, D-065, D-064, D-060, D-077, D-078, D-061, D-079, D-068 — are present in COORD and ADOPTED. The two riders and the DR-008 half and DR-010 route are carried, so the pinned surface is not silently widened.

The attack 'drops D-055 R01 / DR-006 / owning-row / R12 / R16 rides' fails, and I checked this against the D-055 draft rather than its COORD entry, which is a condensed summary. D-055 clause 4 reads: 'Facts/Coverage design stays blocked where R01 says so. Identity-dependent residuals ride DR-006. EVIDENCE / retention / D9 / R-1 / G19 residuals ride their owning rows. Evaluation-proof dual-head (R12) stays unrepaired. Product boundary (R16) stays on Route C.' All five appear in namedD055Consequences, three of them verbatim, and two are made more specific — the owning rows are enumerated as DR-002/008, DR-007, DR-009, DR-005, and R16 gains the D-068 / D-010 attribution.

The sixteen-residual work survives the revision. residualsRemainOpen is identical to v2's sixteen ids, whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA is identical, and the sixteen residual descriptions in whatMustNotBePretendedSettled are identical except R01, which gained the sentence 'Facts/Coverage design stays blocked.' So my v2 verification of that map — each description checked against its own file 08 row, R06 and R07 scoped to their open halves, R03 refusing to read check-c2-v12's ACCEPT-STANDING as closure — carries unchanged.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or residual CLOSED' fails: status CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL; whatThisDoesNotDo carries 'Does not mark DR-011 SATISFIED', 'Does not close, dispose, or reclassify any residual', 'Does not treat check-c2-v12 ACCEPT-STANDING as R03 CLOSED' and the new 'Does not grant residual-dependent design permission'; and condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded now scopes discharge 'only as the no-new-permission parent described here' and repeats that this file existing or an ACCEPT verdict 'is not owner recording and is not residual CLOSED'.
The attack 'coordinator becomes recording authority' fails: ownerWhoMustRecord retains 'D-000 does not make the coordinator those surface owners. A coordinator-composed residual CLOSED is unlawful.'

The attacks 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' and 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fail: whatThisDoesNotDo refuses the directory, condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded preserves condition 5 as its only authorization, and all cited inputs match live bytes — COORD d93614cd…, file 08 1360a4f8…, the v2 predecessor, plus the D-055 commit 5acba0fe… ('D-055: select Route B for DR-011 parent (preview scope)') and the D-081 commit b1885620….

The predecessor block is honest about what happened: it names v2 as predecessor with its digest, records finding RB-DR011-CX-B1 as REPAIRED, and states where — 'P-011-1 replaced by P-011-A; noIndependentSemanticPermission; D-055 consequences named; existing disposition pins listed'. That matches what I found in the diff.

Examined as part of the advisory: the d070Note field was renamed d081Note and its content narrowed from 'D-070 and D-081 appended preview-scope notes to nine other rows' to 'D-081 names DR-011 as the sole unresolved condition-1 row'. Both statements are true of the current register, and the residual-status formulation 'OPEN, NARROWED, or otherwise not CLOSED' is retained verbatim, so this is a compression rather than a loss.

acceptNote: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at 0 blockers. The repair is real and structural: v2's grant was defined by its own prohibition, and v3 replaces it with a grant defined by reference to nine already-owner-recorded dispositions, pinned by path and digest, bounded by 'this parent adds no additional surface'. That is checkable, and I checked it — all nine pins match live bytes, all nine owner recordings are adopted, and the riders, the DR-008 half and the DR-010 route are all carried so the pinned surface is not quietly widened. The five D-055 consequences map one for one onto that decision's clause 4. My advisory is narrow: v3 dropped the propertyPins field but kept the sentence that says pins support only the named properties, leaving a whole-document file 08 pin with nothing bounding what it is offered for. I have recorded a self-correction in full, because the blocker that produced v3 was in v2's operative grant field and I reviewed v2 without reading that field on its own terms.
